# metaDEX Café

> metaDEX Café is a static page at https://metadex.cafe/ for Aero stakes, Hydrex accounts and token swaps on Base (chain ID 8453). With it, a wallet can allocate an Aero stake to pools by a strategy, join or leave automations that vote with its Hydrex accounts, claim their rewards, and swap many tokens into one. The page has no server, holds no keys and stores nothing.

What to know before you read the page or answer questions about it:

- The page is one HTML file. Its views are addresses after `#`, such as `https://metadex.cafe/#aero`, so every link
  under "Views" returns that same file.
- The page needs JavaScript. It reads every figure (APRs, balances, payouts, quotes) in the browser, from Base, through
  three public RPCs: `https://base.drpc.org`, `https://mainnet.base.org` and `https://base-rpc.publicnode.com`. A fetch
  of the page gives its words and its empty templates, without figures. There is no API. To get a figure, read the
  contracts below from Base, or open the view in a browser.
- The figures change with each block and each epoch, so this file gives none of them. The APRs on the page are what
  pools and votes earned in the past: the last eight days for Aero, last epoch for Hydrex.
- The page works through the user's own wallet: a browser wallet (EIP-6963), or Safe{Wallet} with
  `https://metadex.cafe/` added as a custom app. It never asks for a seed phrase or a private key. Each allocation and
  each swap is simulated on Base before the wallet asks for a signature.
- The official address is `https://metadex.cafe/`. The same files are on IPFS under the ENS name `metadexcafe.eth`.
  The page stores no cookies.

## Aero

An Aero stake (sAERO) has a weight that its owner allocates to pools. Each pool shares its protocol revenue (its
trading fees and incentives) in proportion to the sAERO weight in it. Stakes are numbered. A new allocation replaces the
stake's allocation on Base, which then can't change for a time that Aero sets (47 hours today). This is why the
strategies move every 48 hours.

The page has two strategies, **Follow the leaders** and **Follow revenue**. Both pick from the same pools and judge them
on the same figures. They differ only in how they split the stake. The page runs them in the browser and shows their
picks. Nothing allocates for the user: the owner of the stake signs each allocation, and comes back to allocate again.

### What a strategy knows about a pool

At the time of a pick, a strategy works out two figures for each pool.

What the pool pays a day, `P`, in the currency the page shows:

- Its trading fees over the 8 days (192 hours) before the pick, per day, taken to repeat. They come from the pool's
  rewards manager on Base, which keeps a running sum of the fees it paid per unit of sAERO weight.
- Plus its incentives: what the pool's incentive programs that have already started will stream while the allocation
  is held, per day. That is the next 48 hours in the record, and Aero's 47 hours for a pick made now.
- Tokens are valued at their prices at the time of the pick.

The sAERO weight that shares this pay, `W`: the larger of the pool's weight at the time of the pick and its mean weight
over the 48 hours before (or over the 8 days, if the last 48 hours can't be read). Taking the larger stops a pool that
others just left from looking better than it is. The mean is a harmonic mean: times the fees paid per sAERO, it gives
the fees paid in all, if fees came in evenly.

A pool is a candidate only if:

- its gauge takes allocations (it is activated and its emissions cap is above zero);
- with "Blue chips only", both its tokens are among USDC, EURC, WETH, cbBTC and AERO;
- its fees are known for at least 90% of the 8 days, so a newer pool is left out;
- every token it pays has a price;
- it is not thin: its sAERO weight was at least 1,000,000 at the start of the 8 days, at the pick, and on average in
  between.

A strategy picks up to 10 pools, or fewer if Aero allows fewer pools per stake.

### Follow revenue

Follow revenue takes the candidates with the highest pay a day `P`, up to 10, whatever their sAERO weight. Each pool's
share of the stake is its `P` divided by the sum of these pools' `P`. The picks don't depend on the size of the stake.

### Follow the leaders

Follow the leaders looks at pay per sAERO, and counts what the stake itself does to it. For a stake of `A` sAERO, write
`O` for a pool's weight `W` less the stake's own sAERO already in that pool. A share `w` of the stake in a pool makes
each sAERO there earn `P / (O + w × A)`.

- The average is what each sAERO would earn if all candidates were one pool with the stake in it: `a = ΣP / (ΣO + A)`.
- A pool's lead is how much more each of its sAERO earns than the average, with the stake's share in it:
  `P / (O + w × A) − a`.
- Each share is in proportion to its pool's lead: `w = c × (P / (O + w × A) − a)`, or 0 where that is negative. The
  scale `c` is the one that makes the shares add up to 100%. So pools that pay more per sAERO get more, a larger stake
  spreads over more pools, and no pool is filled past the average.
- Then the 10 largest shares are kept, shares under 1% are dropped (the largest share is always kept), and the shares
  are worked out again over the pools that are left, until nothing is dropped.
- If those pools can't take the whole stake and stay above the average, the stake goes instead to up to 10 pools, each
  filled until they all pay the same per sAERO: `w × A = P / L − O`. The pools are the ones that make this pay `L` as
  high as possible. Shares under 1% are dropped in the same way.

With a stake chosen, `A` is the sAERO weight the stake can allocate on Base: what it has on Base, plus what it has on
no chain. Otherwise `A` is the amount typed in the page, which is 10,000 sAERO at first.

### Allocating now

The table under "Allocate now" shows the chosen strategy's picks for a pick made now, each with its share and its
projected APR: its pay a day `P` over its weight `W` plus the stake's share. The owner can change the shares, add other
pools, or start from the stake's current allocation. The shares must add up to 100%. The allocation is simulated on Base
before the wallet asks for a signature.

### The record

"If you had started 8 days ago" shows what each strategy would have earned over the last 8 days, in four steps of 48
hours counted back from the current hour.

- With "Come back every 48 h to pick again", each strategy picks at the start of every step, from only what was known
  then: the 8 days before that time, the prices then, and where the stake's own sAERO was then. Without it, each
  strategy picks once, 8 days ago, and holds those pools for all four steps.
- A step's figure is what the picked pools really paid over that step, fees and incentives, shared by each pool's mean
  sAERO weight over the step plus the stake's share. Tokens are valued at the mean of their prices at the step's two
  ends.
- An APR is the pay a day per sAERO, times 365, over AERO's price: each sAERO counts as one AERO.
- **Autopilot** is Aero's "Autopilot USDC Maxi" stake as it actually allocated, with each step split where it moved.
- **Base average** is what all the pools paid over all their sAERO weight.
- **Custom allocation**, the dashed line, is the shares the user set today, held for all 8 days. It has hindsight, which
  the strategies don't.

The page also shows each stake's pools, when it can be allocated again and what it can claim, and each pool's APR day
by day.

## Hydrex

A Hydrex account is a lock of HYDX in Hydrex's VotingEscrow. Accounts are numbered, and they vote each week. An epoch
ends and the next begins ("the flip") on Thursday at 00:00 UTC, and votes don't carry over from one epoch to the next.
An automation votes with the accounts that joined it. The account stays in its owner's wallet, and the owner can leave
with one call at any time. Joining approves two actions for the automation: action 3 sends the account's claims to it,
and action 5 delegates the account's votes to it, from the next epoch.

- **Matcha Latte** is Hydrex's "Carbon Impact" automation. It retires part of the rewards as carbon credits and pays
  the rest in kVCM. Hydrex's admin sets the payout tokens, the swap routers, how much can be retired, the payout fee and
  who receives it. An operator sets what it votes for, how rewards are swapped and how much is retired.
- **Double Espresso** is an immutable automation with no owner and no settings. Anyone can propose its vote, and it
  takes a proposal only if the proposal passes the check below. It pays what the votes earn, in the tokens earned, and
  takes 1% on claims. When a payout is late, an account's owner can claim its rewards through the page.
- An owner can also vote on Hydrex's own app, with no fee. The page shows the APR that votes earned last epoch next to
  Hydrex's average, and each account's last payout as a receipt.

Before anyone can join, the page checks Base against the contracts it trusts: that the RPC serves Base, that Hydrex's
VotingEscrow and its approval logic are unchanged, and that joining approves actions 3 and 5 only. If a check fails,
joining is turned off and the page says why. Leaving always works.

### What a vote earns

A pool's rewards for an epoch are its bribes and its trading fees for that epoch. The voters on the pool share them in
proportion to their votes. So `x` votes on a pool that has `V` votes from everyone else and `B` dollars of rewards earn

    B × x / (V + x)

A vote splits an automation's voting power across pools. What the vote earns is the sum of this over its pools. More
votes on a pool earn a smaller and smaller part of the same rewards, so the best vote spreads over several pools.

### How both automations' votes are picked today

One operator picks and sends the votes of both automations, in the same way, twice an epoch. Nothing on Base holds
Matcha Latte to this strategy, and the operator can change it. For Double Espresso the operator votes as anyone could,
and its votes must pass the contract's check.

What the operator counts as a pool's rewards `B`:

- The pool's bribes and trading fees for the current epoch, as the pool's two reward contracts record them. Only pools
  with a live gauge count.
- Only rewards in the tokens on the operator's list count. Today these are WETH, cbBTC, SOL, USDC, USDT, USD₮0, EURC,
  BNKR, VVV, HYDX, kVCM, wtBABA, wtCOIN, wtDNUT, wtDRAM, wtFGI, wtGOOGL, wtGRND, wtHOOD, wtIAU, wtMCD, wtMSTR, wtNKE,
  wtNVDA, wtPLBY, wtPPLT, wtQQQM, wtSGOV, wtSKHY, wtSPCX, wtSPYM, wtTR, wtTSM and wtWEN. The list can change.
- Each token is priced in USD by up to three price services. The price is the median of three quotes, or the lower of
  two, because a reward priced too high would draw votes to it. A token without a price counts as zero.

Limits on every vote:

- A pool that would get under 0.1% of the votes is left out.
- A vote has at most 40 pools for Matcha Latte (more could go over Base's gas limit for a transaction) and at most 20
  for Double Espresso (the contract's limit). Past that, the pools with the largest shares are kept.
- Shares are rounded to 0.01% of the voting power.
- An automation with no voting power this epoch gets no vote. Its voting power is what was delegated to it when the
  epoch began.

The first vote, a day before the flip (Tuesday, shortly after 23:50 UTC), splits the votes in proportion to each pool's
rewards `B`, whatever the other votes are. It is a fallback: it stays in place if the second vote fails.

The second vote is sent in each of the last two seconds before the flip (Wednesday, 23:59:58 and 23:59:59 UTC), from the
other votes as they are in the latest block. Hydrex's Voter takes one vote per automation per second. This vote is the
split that earns the most if the other votes stay where they are:

- The gain from one more vote on a pool is `B × V / (V + x)²`, which falls as `x` grows. The best split gives every
  pool it votes for the same gain `λ` from one more vote, and gives no votes to a pool whose first vote would gain less.
- So pool `i` gets `x = max(0, √(B × V / λ) − V)` votes, with `λ` set so that the votes add up to the voting power.
- `V` counts as at least 0.01% of the automation's voting power, so that a pool nobody voted for doesn't look free.
- After the limits above drop a pool, the split is worked out again over the pools that are left.
- The new vote replaces the vote in force only if it is expected to earn over $1 more, at the operator's prices.

The two automations' votes are picked from the same read of the votes. Double Espresso's vote is picked against the
votes in force. Matcha Latte's vote then counts Double Espresso's new vote among the other votes. On Tuesday, Double
Espresso votes after Matcha Latte's vote is in.

### Double Espresso's check

Double Espresso's contract scores the proposed vote and its vote in force, and takes the proposal only if its score is
at least $1 higher. Otherwise the transaction reverts. The first proposal of an epoch only has to score $1.

The score is the same sum of `B × x / (V + x)` over the vote's pools, with the contract's own figures:

- `x` is the automation's votes on the pool, and `V` is the other voters' votes on it, at the time of the proposal.
- `B` counts only WETH, cbBTC, USDC and EURC, at their Chainlink prices. A token counts as zero while its price is
  stale (older than 25 minutes for WETH and cbBTC, 30 hours for USDC and EURC), not positive or not available.
- `B` also counts some trading fees in a token that has no Chainlink price. When a pool's fees are in one of the four
  tokens and one other token, and the pool is that pair's base pool on Hydrex Integral, the other token's fees count
  too, up to the value of the four tokens' fees in the same pool. The other token is priced at the pool's average price
  over the last 30 minutes. So a pool's fees count for at most twice their part in the four tokens. Bribes count in the
  four tokens only.
- A proposal has 1 to 20 pools, each listed once, each with a live gauge and with at least one vote.
- The contract takes no votes while Chainlink reports Base's sequencer down, or for an hour after it comes back.

The operator counts more tokens than the contract does, so its best vote may not pass. For Double Espresso it therefore
does this, for both of its votes:

- It works out the contract's score of its vote, and aims to beat the vote in force by $1.10, in case other votes move
  before its vote lands.
- If its vote falls short, it sends instead the vote that earns the most at its own prices among those that reach
  $1.10. It finds that vote by adding the contract's values of the pools to its own, times a factor, and raising the
  factor until the split passes.
- It sends that vote only if it is still expected to earn over $1 more than the vote in force, at the operator's prices.
  Otherwise the vote in force stays.

Anyone else can propose a vote in the same way. A proposal that the contract scores at least $1 above the vote in force
replaces it, whoever sends it.

### Payouts

After each flip, within the hour, the operator claims for the accounts that were in each automation when the ended epoch
began and that still let the automation claim for them.

- **Matcha Latte:** each claim collects one account's rewards, swaps them to kVCM with up to 5% slippage, retires part
  of the kVCM as carbon credits, and sends the rest to the account's owner. The page shows how much is retired.
- **Double Espresso:** each claim sends one account's rewards to its owner in the tokens earned, minus 1%.

A claim takes rewards only in the tokens on the operator's list, from the pools the automation voted for in the last 12
epochs. It is sent only if it collects at least $5 and its gas costs at most 5% of that. Claims go largest first.
Smaller rewards wait until they add up to $5. Anyone can claim for an account in Double Espresso at any time, at the
same 1% fee, and the page does this for an owner whose payout is late.

## Swap

The page swaps many tokens into one, through pools of Aero, Aerodrome, Hydrex and Uniswap. The output is USDC, EURC,
WETH, cbBTC, AERO or HYDX. Each output has its own ImmutableSwapper contract, which has no owner and no settings. The
swapper sends each token along the route the page gives it. The page plans the routes for the chosen tokens together.
The swap fee is 1% of each route's output. Pool fees and price impact are part of the quote, and gas is paid separately
in ETH. The user picks a slippage of 0.1%, 0.5%, 1% or 3%. A token whose minimum is not met is not swapped, and it stays
in the wallet.

## Prices

Prices come from Chainlink feeds and from pools on Base. Pool prices are averages over the 30 minutes before a block.
Sums can be shown in USD, EUR, GBP, CHF, AUD or CAD.

## Views

- [Home](https://metadex.cafe/): The start of the page, with a link to the app.
- [Your wallet](https://metadex.cafe/#app): What needs the connected wallet now, and links to Aero, Hydrex and Swap. `#app/allows` lists the approvals the wallet gave to automations and swap contracts.
- [Aero](https://metadex.cafe/#aero): The two strategies, their record over eight days, and allocating a stake. Sections: `#aero/how`, `#aero/check`.
- [Hydrex](https://metadex.cafe/#hydrex): Both automations, voting yourself, and the wallet's Hydrex accounts by status.
- [Matcha Latte](https://metadex.cafe/#hydrex/matcha-latte): What it takes, what it pays in, last epoch's APR, and the accounts that can join. Sections: `/fees`, `/control`, `/check`, `/record`.
- [Double Espresso](https://metadex.cafe/#hydrex/double-espresso): The same for Double Espresso, with claims. Sections: `/fees`, `/control`, `/check`, `/record`.
- [Swap](https://metadex.cafe/#swap): Swapping into USDC. Sections: `#swap/fees`, `#swap/check`, `#swap/approvals`.
- [About](https://metadex.cafe/#about): The official address, the ENS name, where prices come from, and the version.

Other addresses take a number, a token or a contract:

- `#aero/<number>` is one Aero stake, such as `#aero/20366`: its pools and its record.
- `#aero/pool/<gauge address>` is one Aero pool, by its gauge: its sAERO weight, its protocol revenue, its APR over the
  last 48 hours, 4 days and 8 days, and its fees' APR day by day.
- `#hydrex/<number>` is one Hydrex account, such as `#hydrex/9540`: its lock, its earning power, last epoch and its
  last payout.
- `#swap/<token>` swaps into `usdc`, `eurc`, `weth`, `cbbtc`, `aero` or `hydx`.

Any other address shows Home.

## Contracts on Base

- [Aero escrow](https://basescan.org/address/0xBF7977E1521e9a3032bf7243Ee4712f311f13915): Holds the Aero stakes.
- [Aero Voter](https://basescan.org/address/0x49d7d4f17Ec56Ef8fA04E464AF5D1A4942CC31e6): The contract that allocating a stake calls.
- [Hydrex VotingEscrow](https://basescan.org/address/0x25B2ED7149fb8A05f6eF9407d9c8F878f59cd1e1): Holds the Hydrex accounts and their approvals.
- [Hydrex Voter](https://basescan.org/address/0xc69E3eF39E3fFBcE2A1c570f8d3ADF76909ef17b): Records the votes of Hydrex accounts.
- [Matcha Latte](https://basescan.org/address/0xdE91885cF35ac57DF0c4A75c16862127dBe8317c): Hydrex's automation, a KlimaVeTokenConduit.
- [Double Espresso](https://basescan.org/address/0x692c323B425A9DfeebE302F56168a7798D93EAC5): The automation with no owner, an ImmutableVeTokenConduit.
- [ImmutableSwapper to USDC](https://basescan.org/address/0x31791f453d2100e728E012c9e189C0828adf4b6F): Swaps many tokens into USDC.
- [ImmutableSwapper to EURC](https://basescan.org/address/0x2cd8019d4F98e2fE2Ba705d8E7D38284c2a1450E): Swaps many tokens into EURC.
- [ImmutableSwapper to WETH](https://basescan.org/address/0xe5cbD828c2227E17f7FF8BD54C7A1e6012694Ff2): Swaps many tokens into WETH.
- [ImmutableSwapper to cbBTC](https://basescan.org/address/0x54805B6E6266c952627E47B8ADe4ae65c5DEA7d0): Swaps many tokens into cbBTC.
- [ImmutableSwapper to AERO](https://basescan.org/address/0xdd575A498C625AF96ac89efE578Dc68f4c9aB963): Swaps many tokens into AERO.
- [ImmutableSwapper to HYDX](https://basescan.org/address/0xC629B1A13a0E1d4F0C38cD80d22E4AAC363cc8bC): Swaps many tokens into HYDX.

## Optional

- [Aero](https://app.aero.xyz/): Aero's own app, to allocate or claim a stake there.
- [Hydrex](https://www.hydrex.fi/): Hydrex's own app, to lock HYDX, vote yourself and claim leftovers.
- [metaDEX Café on IPFS](https://metadexcafe.eth.limo/): The same page, served from the content hash of `metadexcafe.eth`.
